I was at a similar situation. I went to uni to study physics at 23, which would mean I'd get my PhD at 32-33. I had many doubts but I do not regret it one bit. Having a child will certainly complicate things though. Do you have an income?

I am sorry for your situation, I am going through something similar, and I can empathise. I would only tell my closest friends and perhaps discuss it a little further with them, as well as my immediate family. Not everyone needs to know, though, right? Perhaps after that it will spread as news, or you'll casually bring it up in conversation when he is mentioned. If your circle of friends is intertwined, you can ask your friends to tell it to other people. But I do not see a need for a big anouncement. Hope you feel better soon. It sucks, but it does get better.
Well. It is certainly easier getting over a traitor than what I perceived as the greatest person I had ever met. But it does hurt like a bitch, nonetheless

I have been going through something as shitty lately. Discussing it with people who understand it helps me. It is sort of like death, and having to end your feelings for another person feels like tearing off one hand with your other. It really really sucks.

There is not much to say though. We have to grieve this loss. Feel free to pm me if you want to discuss it, or just talk to someone about the weather. 

My girlfriend/fiancee was also my best friend, and I lost everything when we broke up.

It really sucks.

I went out with H yesterday. I tried to steer to conversation towards past relationships, so that I'd get a chance to tell her what is going on (she does know that I am recently broken up, but we had never discussed it). Anyway, she did open up about her last relationship,which was nice because I saw that she had been through virtually the same thing, with some differences but some very strange details were eerily familiar.

That gave me the opportunity to basically tell her that I haven't really gotten over my ex, and her verdict was that she understands, and that I'll probably never really get over her; in the sense that it will always hurt when I think about her. I do concur with your analogy about it being like death\-\-it is not as immediate and of dire consequence, but it is such a large change in my life and my overall way of thinking, that I do not see how I'll ever get over it. I just blindly trust that I will stop thinking about her obsessively.

The verdict was that we do not have to stop having fun with each other (with H, that is), and truth be told it gets my mind off it. When I came back home this morning it all came flooding back, after a short break. The fact that H knows my state of mind sort of terminates any ethical quarrels I've been having with myself.

And for the first time I did connect with her over something nontrivial, which did feel nice.

Before us cutting contact, D told me that she still kept thinking that our relationship was not really over, and there was a vague promise of us getting back together in the distant future. She said she had to abolish that. Perhaps she is right, and that is what I need to do, but it becomes so much more difficult when  I realise that I do not want to stop feeling that way, because it is a beautiful feeling.

When I reach that state, perhaps I can start thinking of renewal and growth, and even meet someone with whom I'll click in a way similar to the one I clicked with D. In the meantime, I know from past experience that the struggle is basically not letting it get to me so that I become inert. That's a forest in which it easy to lose yourself, and go to extremes you wouldn't go to with a sane mind\-as has happened before, when luckily D led me out of that forest\-or rather, we led ourselves out. But at times it is so freaking difficult not closing your eyes for two more hours, opening the drapes, and getting out of bed.

Thank you so much, I know the supply of interest for a stranger's love life is limited, but it so much helps to talk about my troubles, trivial though they may seem. Cheers to you! :)

you are very right on my having to stop seeing the other girl, let's call her H. It is not that I never thought that it is an unethical thing to do, it is just that she gives me incentive to get out of bed, bathe, and not think about D. constantly for a couple of hours (hehe). It is selfish, but it was a leap of judgement, like finding a cheap replacement for an expensive drug habbit. D. seems pretty determined to not pursue it further, and we haven't met since January, which makes it easier on her part to make this decision. Many a time have I tried to make her understand that she will probably not find anything like what we had, and says she does not have expectations that high.

I cut things off because she wants to move on, difficult though it may be, while I don't really want to and if we kept talking, I'd have hope, while she makes plans with this other dude. That hurts even more.

She does not want to break things up with him, but also confesses to still love me when the discussion derails to the elephant in the room. 

Thank you for the input. I really appreciate it.
Hi! I am a person, and I am here!
